claims.statement: Tom Allen was one of the party on the steamer Lady Pike for the excursion from St. Louis to Carroll Island, Illinois, on 25 January 1870.
Tom Allen was a resident of St. Louis in March 1870.
Tom Allen was preparing to leave St. Louis for New Orleans to engage Jem Mace.
Tom Allen was to travel to New Orleans in May 1870, with Joe Coburn accompanying him.
Mrs. Allen left St. Louis on Thursday to join her husband in New Orleans.
Tom Allen and Jem Mace were still at New Orleans.
Tom Allen arrived in St. Louis with Mace's agent Abrahams.
Tom Allen had completed an eastern tour and was expected back in St. Louis on the morning of July 2, 1870.
Tom Allen (printed as 'Thomas Allens') followed Mace's party to Wyandotte with Billy Carroll, W. D. Lonergan, Charles Brownfield and Jack Goulding.
The correspondent met Tom Allen at Sedalia, Missouri, a few days before June 9, 1871, and Allen handed him one of his cards.
Tom Allen of St. Louis arrived in Kansas City with Jem Mace and Jim Cusick for the Mace-Coburn fight.
Allen and the party took rooms at the St. Nicholas Hotel in Kansas City.
Tom Allen arrived in Kansas City on June 1, 1871 with Jem Mace, Dick Hollywood and Jim Cusick for the Mace-Coburn fight.
Tom Allen went with Jem Mace's party to Westford on June 2, 1871, where the ring was staked out on the Gillis farm and Joe Coburn did not appear.
Tom Allen and Jem Mace were due to arrive from Kansas City that morning.
Tom Allen said he had returned to St. Louis from the Mace-Coburn fight the day before.
Tom Allen gave his address as 417 Washington Avenue, St. Louis, in January 1872.
Tom Allen left St. Louis for Detroit with Jack Looney and two or three others to see the Mace and O'Baldwin fight.
Tom Allen was a resident of St. Louis when he beat Mike McCoole in 1873.
Tom Allen had a house at 417 Washington avenue, St. Louis, where a deposit was to be put up.
Tom Allen and Mike McCoole were both residents of St. Louis.
A deposit for the match was to be put up at Tom Allen's house, 417 Washington Avenue, on July 8, 1873.
Tom Allen signed a letter dated October 23, 1873 from the Mount Olive House, St. Louis County (printed as 'Moun? OLIvE Howse').
Tom Allen was staying and training at the Eight-Mile House, taking things easily before the Hogan fight.
Tom Allen was staying at the Eight-Mile House, where he trained with his trainer and Arthur Chambers.
Tom Allen left the Eight-Mile House for the fighting ground on October 26, 1873, with Arthur Chambers and Jack Madden.
Tom Allen was already in the vicinity of the fighting ground, having left on Sunday morning, October 26, 1873.
Tom Allen came back to St. Louis the night of the failed Hogan fight and met a reporter in the direction of Looney's resort.
Dr. C. E. Tennent came out to see Tom Allen while Allen was working near Omaha, before the Hogan fight.
Tom Allen arrived in Kansas City with Arthur Chambers, and his trainer Jack Madden joined them.
After Omaha men threatened to shoot them, Tom Allen and Jack Looney left Omaha for Kansas City, reaching it safely on Friday, November 21.
Tom Allen went from St. Louis to Springfield, Illinois, in 1874 to attend the dedication of the National Lincoln Monument and the Army of the Tennessee reunion.
Tom Allen was said to propose a speculating tour of his native country, which was the cause of the anticipated match with Mace.
Tom Allen said he came to St. Louis to live and means to stay there.
Tom Allen returned to St. Louis on 15 August 1874 from the Edwards-Collyer fight near Pittsburg, Pennsylvania.
Tom Allen earlier travelled to New York hunting Ben Hogan, who had offered to fight him, and returned saying Hogan evaded the meeting.
Tom Allen arrived in Newark, met Jim Coyne there, and went on to New York.
In New York Tom Allen was to be the guest of Harry Hill.
Tom Allen went East to arrange the preliminaries for a fight with George Rooke, despite his retirement and his recent denial of the match.
Tom Allen returned to St. Louis from a visit to the principal cities of the East.
Tom Allen planned to leave St. Louis in two or three weeks and go into training.
Tom Allen was training at McKee's Rocks for the match with George Rooke in May 1875.
Tom Allen planned to go to Pittsburg on Sunday night, training at McKee's Rocks and using French's, 54 Tenth Street, as headquarters.
Tom Allen was living in St. Louis in June 1875.
Tom Allen trained for the Rooke fight at a farmhouse on the Ohio River near Pittsburg, with Arthur Chambers.
Tom Allen left Pittsburg on Friday, June 18, 1875, and arrived back in St. Louis the next morning.
Tom Allen was living a quiet life on Washington avenue in the autumn of 1875.
Tom Allen arrived in Chicago from St. Louis on November 17, 1875.
Tom Allen planned to stay in Chicago for a couple of days after the match was made.
